label: browsing
definition: A person visibly inspects displayed items or information, looking over them or moving between them.
counter_examples: Simply passing through or remaining still without visible inspection.

label: leaving_baggage
definition: A person puts down or leaves baggage and moves away without it; a remaining bag and visible departure can support the event.
counter_examples: Carrying a bag throughout or only briefly adjusting it.

label: drop_down
definition: A person visibly loses balance or support and drops or collapses to the floor.
counter_examples: Deliberate bending, sitting, or controlled lying down without a fall.

label: shop_exit
definition: A person crosses a visible shop entrance from the shop interior to outside.
counter_examples: Walking past the entrance or entering the shop.

label: hugging
definition: People embrace by placing their arms around one another with close torso contact.
counter_examples: Passing close by, fighting or a brief hand touch alone.

label: leaving_object
definition: A person leaves an object behind and moves away without it; visible object placement followed by departure supports this event.
counter_examples: An object merely resting in the scene with no observed leaving action.

label: shaking_hands_with_somebody
definition: Two people extend hands, grasp each other's hand and perform a greeting handshake.
counter_examples: Other hand interactions, pointing or exchanging an object without a handshake.

label: browsing_newspaper
definition: A person visibly reads or looks through a newspaper, including holding and inspecting its pages.
counter_examples: Browsing other items or merely carrying folded paper.

label: shaking_hands_with_someone
definition: Two people extend hands, grasp each other's hand and perform a greeting handshake.
counter_examples: Other hand interactions, pointing or exchanging an object without a handshake.

label: shop_enter
definition: A person crosses a visible shop entrance from outside into the shop interior.
counter_examples: Walking past the entrance or leaving the shop.

label: running
definition: A person moves with a running gait, faster strides and a visible flight phase or clear jogging motion.
counter_examples: Ordinary walking, camera motion, or stationary leg movement.

label: lie_down
definition: A person deliberately transitions from standing or sitting to a reclining or lying position.
counter_examples: An uncontrolled fall, bending down, or already lying still without a transition.

label: meeting
definition: People come together and visibly engage with one another, such as stopping to converse or greet.
counter_examples: Merely crossing paths or unrelated nearby walking.

label: walking
definition: A person moves on foot with an ordinary walking gait.
counter_examples: Standing, running, or motion caused only by the camera.

label: immobile
definition: A person remains in the same position without locomotion across the visible observation interval.
counter_examples: Walking, running or briefly slowing while continuing to move.

label: drinking_coffee
definition: A person brings a cup or similar drink container to their mouth and visibly drinks; coffee identity may be uncertain from pixels and must not be invented.
counter_examples: Merely holding a cup or touching the face.

label: vehicle_stops
definition: A visible vehicle transitions from moving to stationary.
counter_examples: A vehicle parked throughout, a pedestrian stopping, or camera motion.
target_hint: The vehicle, not a nearby person.

label: person_picks_up_object
definition: A person lifts an object from the ground or a supporting surface and takes possession of it.
counter_examples: Bending without an object or putting an object down.

label: person_opens_vehicle_door
definition: A person moves a vehicle door from closed toward open.
counter_examples: A door already open, closing a door or opening a building door.

label: person_exits_vehicle
definition: A person visibly moves from inside a vehicle to outside it.
counter_examples: Standing near a vehicle or entering it.

label: person_talks_on_phone
definition: A person holds or uses a phone in a visible calling posture, usually near the ear or mouth.
counter_examples: Only texting or reading a phone, or touching an ear without a phone.

label: person_exits_scene_through_structure
definition: A person exits the visible scene through a doorway, gate or other structural opening.
counter_examples: Moving out of the image at an ordinary frame boundary without a structural opening.

label: person_enters_scene_through_structure
definition: A person enters the visible scene through a doorway, gate or other structural opening.
counter_examples: Appearing at an ordinary frame boundary or already being inside the scene.

label: person_closes_facility_door
definition: A person moves a building or facility door from open toward closed.
counter_examples: Closing a vehicle door or walking through an already closed door area.

label: vehicle_turns_right
definition: A moving vehicle changes heading to its own right through a visible turn.
counter_examples: Straight motion, merely moving rightward in the image, or turning left.
target_hint: The vehicle; direction is relative to its previous heading.

label: person_carries_heavy_object
definition: A person carries an object with visible weight-bearing effort, such as a strained posture or two-handed supported load.
counter_examples: Ordinary small-item carrying without visible evidence of weight or effort.

label: person_stands_up
definition: A person transitions from a sitting, crouching or lying posture into standing.
counter_examples: Already standing, ordinary walking or sitting down.

label: vehicle_makes_u_turn
definition: A vehicle makes a near-180-degree turn and proceeds in approximately the opposite direction.
counter_examples: A simple left or right turn or straight reversing.
target_hint: The turning vehicle, not a person.

label: person_embraces_person
definition: One person embraces another with arms around the other person and close torso contact.
counter_examples: A handshake, passing close by, or physical fighting alone.

label: person_closes_door
definition: A person moves a visible door from open toward closed; the public label does not specify whether it is a vehicle or facility door.
counter_examples: Opening a door, standing near an already closed door or assuming a door type not visible.

label: vehicle_drops_off_person
definition: A visible vehicle arrives or stops and a person visibly exits it and departs from the vehicle.
counter_examples: A parked vehicle with no visible exit, a person merely walking nearby, or a person entering a vehicle.
target_hint: Scene-level vehicle and exit interaction; do not invent a vehicle identity or bind it to a pedestrian box.

label: vehicle_turns_left
definition: A moving vehicle changes heading to its own left through a visible turn.
counter_examples: Straight motion, merely moving leftward in the image, turning right or camera motion.
target_hint: The vehicle; direction is relative to its previous heading, not the image axes.

label: vehicle_starts
definition: A visible vehicle transitions from stationary to moving.
counter_examples: A vehicle already moving throughout, a pedestrian starting to walk, or camera motion.
target_hint: The vehicle at scene level; no reliable vehicle track identity is provided.

label: person_leaves_shop_window
definition: A person disengages from looking at a shop-window display and visibly moves away from that window.
counter_examples: Merely passing a shop window without viewing it or exiting a shop doorway without evidence of leaving a window display.

label: window_shopping
definition: A person stands or moves slowly while visibly inspecting merchandise displayed through a shop window.
counter_examples: Merely walking past the window, looking elsewhere or browsing inside a shop rather than at its window display.

label: vehicle_reverses
definition: A visible vehicle moves backward relative to its own heading.
counter_examples: Forward motion toward the camera, movement down the image, a U-turn or camera motion alone.
target_hint: The reversing vehicle at scene level; do not substitute a nearby person's identity.

label: person_talks_to_person
definition: A person visibly interacts with another person in a conversation-like exchange, supported by facing, mouth movement or communicative gestures.
counter_examples: Merely standing near another person, passing by or assuming spoken words from silent footage.

label: person_texts_on_phone
definition: A person visibly types or taps on a handheld phone in a texting-like posture.
counter_examples: Only holding a phone, calling with the phone at the ear or inventing the message content.

label: hand_interacts_with_person
definition: A person visibly uses a hand to physically interact with another person, such as touching, greeting by hand or a hand-to-hand exchange. The hand action and its connection to the other person must be visible.
counter_examples: Mere proximity, gesturing in empty space, handling only an unrelated object, or assuming hand contact hidden by occlusion.
target_hint: The visible people involved in the hand interaction; do not invent a separate hand identity.

label: person_closes_trunk
definition: A person visibly moves a vehicle trunk lid or rear cargo hatch from open toward closed.
counter_examples: A trunk closed throughout, opening a trunk, closing a passenger door or reaching into the cargo area without closing its lid.
target_hint: The person visibly closing the trunk or rear cargo hatch.

label: person_closes_vehicle_door
definition: A person visibly moves a vehicle passenger door from open toward closed.
counter_examples: A vehicle door already closed, opening a door, closing a facility door or closing only a trunk lid.
target_hint: The person acting on the visible vehicle passenger door.

label: person_loads_vehicle
definition: A person visibly transfers an object from outside a vehicle into its passenger or cargo area. The object transfer into the vehicle must be visible.
counter_examples: A person entering without an object, removing an object from the vehicle, standing nearby or carrying an object past it.
target_hint: The visible person moving the object into the vehicle.

label: person_opens_facility_door
definition: A person visibly moves a building or facility door from closed toward open.
counter_examples: A facility door already open, walking through without opening it, closing it or opening a vehicle door.
target_hint: The person visibly acting on the building or facility door.

label: person_opens_trunk
definition: A person visibly moves a vehicle trunk lid or rear cargo hatch from closed toward open.
counter_examples: A trunk open throughout, closing its lid, opening a passenger door or reaching into an already open cargo area.
target_hint: The person visibly opening the trunk or rear cargo hatch.

label: person_purchases
definition: A person visibly takes part in a purchase transaction, supported by a payment-related action involving money, a card or a payment device together with an exchange of goods or a seller/counter interaction. Transaction details and amounts are not inferred.
counter_examples: Conversation alone, browsing, carrying goods, a hand-to-hand exchange without purchase evidence or inventing a payment hidden from view.
target_hint: The visible person making the purchase, supported by visible transaction evidence.

label: person_puts_down_object
definition: A person visibly lowers and releases an object onto the ground or another supporting surface. Moving away afterward is not required.
counter_examples: Picking an object up, adjusting it while retaining hold, an object resting throughout or assuming an unseen placement.
target_hint: The person visibly placing and releasing the object.

label: person_reads_document
definition: A person visibly looks at and reads or inspects a paper document, pages or a printed text item, held in the hands or resting on a surface. The written contents need not be readable and must not be invented.
counter_examples: Merely carrying folded paper, reading only a phone, looking elsewhere or assuming reading without visible attention to a document.
target_hint: The visible person attending to the document or pages.

label: person_rides_bicycle
definition: A person visibly sits or stands astride a bicycle and travels with it in a riding posture, with pedaling or clear bicycle movement supporting the action.
counter_examples: Walking a bicycle, standing beside it, carrying it, sitting stationary without riding evidence or riding a motorcycle.
target_hint: The person riding the visible bicycle; do not use a vehicle-only identity.

label: person_sits_down
definition: A person visibly transitions from standing or another raised posture into a seated posture on a chair, bench, ground or other support.
counter_examples: Already sitting throughout, standing up, bending while remaining on the feet, an uncontrolled fall or assuming a hidden sitting transition.
target_hint: The person undergoing the visible transition into sitting.

label: person_talks_to_phone
zh_name: 对手机通话（公开标签措词）
definition: The public label wording is person talks to phone. A person visibly uses a phone in a calling posture, such as holding it near the mouth or ear with speaking-like behavior. Audio, spoken words and conversation contents are not inferred.
counter_examples: Only texting or reading a phone, merely carrying it, touching the face without a visible phone or inventing speech from silent footage.
target_hint: The visible person using the phone in a calling posture; retain this exact public label.

label: vehicle_picks_up_person
definition: A visible vehicle receives a person who approaches and visibly enters it as part of a pickup interaction. A subsequent vehicle departure may support the event but is not required if boarding is visible.
counter_examples: A person merely walking near a vehicle, exiting it, a vehicle parked without visible boarding or assuming someone entered behind an occlusion.
target_hint: Scene-level vehicle and boarding interaction; no person subject binding or invented vehicle track identity.
